The core duality lies in the mechanical distinction between walking and running: heel-strike dominance versus toe-off dynamics. This creates a fundamental performance gap—walking takes 25 minutes longer per mile. The primitive 'heel_strike_differential' encodes this via time-based kinematic disparity. However, deceptive practices like limp manipulation exploit biomechanical subtleties, violating the implicit assumption of fair play. The 'limp_deception' primitive models how a slight deviation in leg angle can yield measurable speed gains. In long-distance events, fatigue management becomes paramount, leading to the adoption of jog-trots—a hybrid gait optimizing energy expenditure. The 'jog_trot_optimization' primitive formalizes this tradeoff between speed and endurance. These primitives form a layered system where GSI ensures fairness through Bayesian inference on gait data, while GSE dynamically adapts motion strategies based on fatigue and kinematic efficiency.
